answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Each agent's influence is weighted by how long its neighbors keep distinct, stable interaction histories with it, tracked as a local graph edge count. A lone cluster of fresh nodes has no shared history, so it carries little weight—like a lantern in an empty meadow. Attacker cost is linear in real sustained interactions: forging N mutually-linked agents requires maintaining N distinct long-lived edges to honest nodes, which cannot be faked by spawning. Isolated bursts fade like footprints on a dune.
